scenes.tts: Structures suggest the channel gains hundreds of square nanometres. A two-state reading of the current says about five. Do they describe the same change?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Sixty-Fold Gap. Two numbers face each other: 300 nm² (structural comparison) and 5 nm² (effective two-state area).
scenes.narration: Structures suggest the channel gains hundreds of square nanometres. A two-state reading of the current says about five. Do they describe the same change?

scenes.tts: Yang and colleagues put purified mouse Pee-AY-zo one into lipid vesicles. Cryo electron microscopy sorted it into two classes, from one sample.
scenes.caption: Yang and colleagues put purified mouse Piezo1 into lipid vesicles. Cryo electron microscopy sorted it into two classes, from one sample.
scenes.visual: A liposome vesicle with Piezo1 particles; the particles sort into two bins. Labels: Yang and colleagues, 2022.
scenes.narration: Yang and colleagues put purified mouse Piezo1 into lipid vesicles. Cryo electron microscopy sorted it into two classes, from one sample.

scenes.tts: One class was curved, the other flattened. Between them was about three hundred square nanometres of in-plane expansion.
scenes.visual: Split screen: curved class (7WLT) and flattened class (7WLU), with 300 nm² beside them.
scenes.narration: One class was curved, the other flattened. Between them was about three hundred square nanometres of in-plane expansion.

scenes.tts: Their abstract hedges whether this rearrangement is the gating transition itself.
scenes.visual: A hedge tag on the flattened class: gating transition? not established.
scenes.narration: Their abstract hedges whether this rearrangement is the gating transition itself.

scenes.tts: Suppose all three hundred square nanometres were coupled to opening. How steep would the current curve be?
scenes.visual: On screen: k = k_B·T_abs / ΔA with ΔA = 300 nm². The measured curve, gentle, waits beside an empty axis.
scenes.narration: Suppose all three hundred square nanometres were coupled to opening. How steep would the current curve be?

scenes.tts: Nearly vertical. The channel would go from ten to ninety percent open over a tiny range of tension.
scenes.visual: Worked on screen: k = k_B·T_abs/ΔA = (4.1 × 10⁻²¹ J)/(300 × 10⁻¹⁸ m²) ≈ 0.014 mN/m; 10 to 90 percent over about 0.06 mN/m. A near-vertical curve is drawn.
scenes.narration: Nearly vertical. The channel would go from ten to ninety percent open over a tiny range of tension.

scenes.tts: The measured curve is about sixty times shallower. The half-activation tensions are of the same order. The slopes are not.
scenes.visual: Overlay: the near-vertical predicted curve on the gentle measured one, 10 to 90 percent over about 3.5 mN/m. Labels: T50 1.9 (calculated from structure) and 2.7 (patch fit), same order; slopes differ about sixty-fold.
scenes.narration: The measured curve is about sixty times shallower. The half-activation tensions are of the same order. The slopes are not.

scenes.tts: Geometry makes a change that large plausible. On paper, an idealized Pee-AY-zo two dome gains about three hundred and ten square nanometres when it flattens.
scenes.caption: Geometry makes a change that large plausible. On paper, an idealized Piezo2 dome gains about three hundred and ten square nanometres when it flattens.
scenes.visual: The idealized cap from the dome chapter flattens again; its 310 nm² ring lights. Tag: different paralog, a calculation.
scenes.narration: Geometry makes a change that large plausible. On paper, an idealized Piezo2 dome gains about three hundred and ten square nanometres when it flattens.

scenes.tts: So why is the measured switch so shallow? The question is open. Here are three testable answers.
scenes.visual: A card with three empty slots, numbered 1 to 3.
scenes.narration: So why is the measured switch so shallow? The question is open. Here are three testable answers.

scenes.tts: First, the dome may not be a two-state switch. If it flattens gradually, like a spring, one area no longer describes it.
scenes.visual: Slot 1 fills: the dome flattens in many small steps, a spring icon beside it. Label: not two states?
scenes.narration: First, the dome may not be a two-state switch. If it flattens gradually, like a spring, one area no longer describes it.

scenes.tts: Second, a patch curve is a population curve. Uneven tension across a patch could spread the half-activation tensions.
scenes.visual: Slot 2 fills: many steep little curves at scattered positions along the tension axis. Tag: illustrative model.
scenes.narration: Second, a patch curve is a population curve. Uneven tension across a patch could spread the half-activation tensions.

scenes.tts: Suppose otherwise identical two-state channels sit at equilibrium and differ only by fixed offsets in half-activation tension. Then averaging broadens their response, and the slope-derived area underestimates their common opening area. Outside that model it is an effective area, not a guaranteed bound. And the published curve also pools different patches.
scenes.visual: The scattered steep curves average into one gentle curve. Label: identical equilibrium switches; common ΔA; fixed T50 offsets; illustrative conditional underestimate. Small note: the published fit pools different patches.
scenes.narration: Suppose otherwise identical two-state channels sit at equilibrium and differ only by fixed offsets in half-activation tension. Then averaging broadens their response, and the slope-derived area underestimates their common opening area. Outside that model it is an effective area, not a guaranteed bound. And the published curve also pools different patches.

scenes.tts: Third, the flattened class may not be the open channel. A structure is not a current recording.
scenes.visual: Slot 3 fills: the flattened structure beside a current trace, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Third, the flattened class may not be the open channel. A structure is not a current recording.

scenes.tts: There is one more twist. In an elasticity model by Haselwandter and MacKinnon, the membrane bends away around the dome.
scenes.visual: Side view: the bilayer around the dome curves away in a wide skirt that reaches well past the protein. Label: footprint, 2018 model.
scenes.narration: There is one more twist. In an elasticity model by Haselwandter and MacKinnon, the membrane bends away around the dome.

scenes.tts: That skirt reaches well past the protein. So tension does work on the footprint as well as on the channel.
scenes.visual: Tension arrows act on the whole skirt as well as on the protein.
scenes.narration: That skirt reaches well past the protein. So tension does work on the footprint as well as on the channel.

scenes.tts: Their numbers are model inputs, not the structural three hundred. Keep the two apart.
scenes.visual: Two cards kept apart: model input, cap about 390 nm², radius 10.2 nm; structural comparison, about 300 nm².
scenes.narration: Their numbers are model inputs, not the structural three hundred. Keep the two apart.

scenes.tts: Neither five square nanometres nor hundreds has been shown to be the area gained on pore opening. The structural expansion is real; which part of it couples to opening is still open.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Open problem. 5 nm² and 300 nm² are both unproven as the opening area. Which part of the flattening opens the pore?
scenes.narration: Neither five square nanometres nor hundreds has been shown to be the area gained on pore opening. The structural expansion is real; which part of it couples to opening is still open.
